title: Oracle simulation of a plain machine
statement: Let $tm$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $x,y$ be words and $t$ a natural number. The oracle machine obtained by embedding $tm$ computes $y$ on input $x$ within $t$ steps relative to $O$ if and only if the run of $tm$ from its initial configuration on $x$ is halted after $t$ steps and has output $y$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A state type and symbol type
A deterministic machine $tm$ with $k$ work tapes
replaced:
Let $M_0$ be a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, let $O$ be any
oracle language, let $x$ and $y$ be words, and let $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  The
oracle machine obtained by embedding $M_0$ computes $y$ on input $x$ within
$t$ steps relative to $O$ if and only if, after running $M_0$ for $t$ steps
from its initial configuration on $x$, the machine has halted and its output
tape holds exactly $y$.  In particular, the input/output behavior and time
bounds of the embedded machine do not depend on the oracle.
